Today, Apple has released updates for the Mac mini and Mac Studio, with both product lines gaining Wi-Fi 7 support for the first time. Below is the complete list of Apple devices that support the full suite of Wi-Fi 7 features.

Operation in the 6 GHz band is not available in all regions.

Apple today published a support document detailing exactly which of its products fully support Wi-Fi 7.

This list differs from Apple's broader list of devices that can connect to Wi-Fi 7 networks, since Wi-Fi 7 is backward compatible.

That means devices limited to Wi-Fi 6E can still join a compatible Wi-Fi 7 network and use the 6 GHz band where it is available, even though they do not support the full feature set of Wi-Fi 7.

Wi-Fi 7 features include 320 MHz channels, 4096-QAM, and Multi-Link Operation (MLO), delivering increased throughput, improved efficiency, and reduced latency — you can learn more about that here.

With that said, here is Apple's official list of devices that support the full suite of Wi-Fi 7 features, as of August 2026:

  • MacBook Pro with the M5 Pro or M5 Max chip or later
  • MacBook Air with the M5 chip or later
  • Mac mini with the M5 Pro chip or later
  • Mac Studio with the M5 Max chip or later
  • iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max or later (excluding iPhone 16e and iPhone 17e)
  • iPhone Air
  • iPad Pro with the M5 chip or later
  • iPad Air with the M4 chip or later

Apple notes that "Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 functionality over the 6 GHz band is available only in countries and regions where that spectrum is permitted for unlicensed Wi-Fi use," adding that "if your country or region hasn't authorised this type of operation, your device will use Wi-Fi over the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands only."
